common_name: Genkai Jishi Leopard Plant (Narrow-Cut Collector Farfugium)

planting.note: Plant container-grown divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in part sun to light shade; Genkai Jishi stays noticeably smaller than most leopard plant selections, so give it a prominent spot near a path or container edge where its finely cut leaf margins can be appreciated up close.

directions: Genkai Jishi is a diminutive Japanese collector's clone of Farfugium japonicum, introduced to American gardens by plantsman Barry Yinger, forming a tidy mound of dark evergreen leaves with narrowly cut, ruffled, serrated margins quite unlike the broad rounded leaves of common leopard plant. Clumps stay compact at roughly a foot tall and a foot and a half wide, making it well suited to container culture or the front of a shaded bed. Spikes of bright yellow daisy-like flowers rise above the foliage starting in mid-fall, drawing late-season butterflies and lasting well as cut flowers. Grow in consistently moist, humus-rich soil in part sun to light shade, sheltering it from hot afternoon exposure.

common_name: Roundabout Fall Leopard Plant (Rounded-Leaf Hybrid Farfugium)

planting.note: Plant container-grown divisions in spring in evenly moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in light open shade, or with only a touch of morning sun; Roundabout Fall tolerates slightly more sun than smooth-leaved leopard plant selections thanks to its thicker leaf texture.

directions: Roundabout Fall is a Juniper Level Botanic Garden hybrid selection crossing Farfugium japonicum var. formosanum with the typical species, chosen for its smaller, thick, distinctly rounded leaves that set it apart from the larger, flatter foliage of most leopard plant cultivars. The compact, dense clump stays evergreen in mild winters and sends up clusters of bright yellow daisy-like flowers in fall. It performs best in light open shade or with only brief morning sun, planted in average to slightly moist, humus-rich soil. Use it as a tidy textural accent along a shaded path edge or in a woodland container planting.
